problem:
If
$u(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]$
and
$v(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]$
are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ find $Aw(t)$ where
$w(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: General Solutions of First-Order Linear Systems of ODEs

feedback.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{3t} \\ 7{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=-2u(t)+7v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-2{e}^{3t})^{′} \\ (7{e}^{5t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6{e}^{3t} \\ 35{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
